1. “DMT vaping” is not the same as “DMT use in Australia”
The strongest evidence says inhalation/smoking is the dominant way people consume N,N-DMT in Australia, but that does not mean modern vape cartridges are the dominant method.
A recent study of 406 people who had inhaled DMT found:
77.6% had used a glass pipe
32.8% had used a bong/water pipe
16.3% had used a rolled joint/cigarette
14.5% reported a vaporizer
Participants could report more than one method of buying DMT vape pens in Australia, so these percentages aren't mutually exclusive. �
PubMed Central (PMC)
So if your research topic says “DMT is the most consumed vape in Australia,” I'd change that claim. A better statement is:
“DMT is predominantly consumed through inhalation in Australia with vaporization representing one of several inhalation methods.”
2. Why is inhalation so prominent?
The main pharmacological reason is the very rapid onset of effects. Research on inhaled DMT describes an experience that develops extremely quickly and is relatively short compared with many other psychedelic experiences. �
Nature +1
An earlier large Global Drug Survey study similarly found that DMT was most often smoked in Australia and described its effects as intense and short-lived. �

This helps explain why inhalation has remained popular among people who choose to use DMT vapes and relatively buying DMT in Australia 
3. Which country stands out?
There isn't enough standardized international data to legitimately say “Country X has the world's highest buying DMT-vaping rate.”
However, Australia is particularly interesting for your research.
A study of 121 Australian recreational DMT vape users found that 98.3% reported smoking DMT. That's an exceptionally high proportion—but remember that the researchers recruited people who were already DMT users, so it does not mean 98.3% of Australians use DMT. �

More recently, Australia's 2025 Ecstasy and Related Drugs Reporting System found that 11% of people who regularly use ecstasy or illicit stimulants reported DMT use in the preceding six months. Again, this is a high-risk/drug-using population, not the general Australian population. �

5. One important distinction for your research
You should separate these four concepts:
DMT prevalence → how many people use DMT
Inhaled DMT → how many DMT users inhale/smoke it
Vaporized DMT → how many specifically use a vaporizer
DMT cartridges → how many use pre-filled vape cartridges
The available scientific literature is much better at measuring the first two than the last two.
That's why I wouldn't claim that the United States, Australia, or any other country has the highest DMT-vape consumption without a dataset specifically measuring vape use.
If you're building this into a research project
A strong research question would be:
“Patterns of N,N-DMT consumption: prevalence, inhalation methods, vaporization, and geographical differences in use.”
You could then investigate Australia vs. United States vs. United Kingdom vs. Canada vs. other countries, while clearly separating general DMT use from vaping.
If you want, I can also �⁠compile a country-by-country table of available DMT statistics and identify which countries have the strongest evidence of DMT use/inhalation, using the most recent studies available.
If this is for a research project, there is an important distinction: DMT is not established as the “most consumed vape.” What the research supports is that inhalation/smoking is the dominant route for DMT, while specifically using a modern vape/e-cigarette appears to be a smaller subset.
What the research shows
A large Global Drug Survey study involving 22,289 respondents found lifetime DMT use of 8.9% among its survey sample and past-year use of 5.0%. Among DMT users, inhalation was the predominant route, at about 92.2%. �
PubMed +1
A more recent study of inhaled DMT users found that a glass pipe was the most commonly reported method (77.6%), followed by a bong/water pipe (32.8%), while a vaporizer was reported by 14.5%. So “inhaled” should not automatically be interpreted as “vaped.” �
PubMed Central (PMC)
In an Australian study of 121 recreational DMT users, 98.3% reported smoking DMT, making smoking by far the dominant route in that particular sample. �
PubMed
For 5-MeO-DMT, which is a different substance from N,N-DMT, one study found that 81% reported smoking/vaporizing as their route. This distinction is important in a research paper because the two substances are frequently conflated. �
PubMed Central (PMC)
Why inhalation/vaporization is common
The pharmacology helps explain the pattern. Inhaled DMT bypasses much of the first-pass metabolism associated with oral administration, producing a rapid onset and relatively short-lived psychedelic experience. �
PubMed Central (PMC) +1
That combination—rapid onset, short duration, and a highly intense subjective effect—helps explain why inhalation is prominent among recreational users. It doesn't mean DMT is the world's most commonly vaped drug, however.
Which country has the highest statistics?
There is no reliable current worldwide ranking showing which country has the highest rate of DMT vaping. The available studies use different populations, years, definitions, and sampling methods, so comparing countries directly would be misleading.
For example, the 2014 Global Drug Survey was an online survey of people interested in or using drugs, rather than a representative population survey. Consequently, its 8.9% lifetime figure should not be interpreted as saying 8.9% of the general population uses DMT. �
PubMed
There are nevertheless useful country-specific studies. Australia, for example, has documented very high rates of smoking among people who had already reported using DMT (98.3%), but that does not establish Australia as the country with the highest prevalence of DMT use. �
PubMed
A strong research conclusion
You could frame your research question as:
“Why is inhalation the predominant route of DMT consumption, and what countries demonstrate the highest prevalence of DMT use?”
That is more scientifically defensible than saying “DMT is the most consumed vape.”
Also, don't confuse DMT prevalence, DMT inhalation prevalence, and DMT-vaping prevalence—they are three different statistics. Current evidence is considerably stronger for the first two than for the third.
If by “most liable” you mean which country appears most likely to have substantial DMT use/vaping, the evidence points toward Australia and the United States, but there is no reliable global ranking specifically for DMT vaping.
Australia: particularly strong evidence of DMT use within drug-using populations. An Australian study found 98.3% of surveyed DMT users smoked it, although this was a specific sample and not the Australian population as a whole. �
PubMed
United States: newer nationally representative research estimates that about 0.8% of U.S. adults used DMT in the past year, equivalent to roughly 2.19 million adults in 2025. �
DOI +1
Australia currently has 11% DMT use among people who regularly use ecstasy or illicit stimulants, according to the 2025 Ecstasy and Related Drugs Reporting System. �
AIHW
So, for a research paper, I'd phrase the conclusion as:
“Australia is one of the countries with particularly strong documented DMT use among established drug-using populations, while the United States has substantial population-level DMT use. However, available evidence does not support naming a single country as having the world's highest rate of DMT vaping.”
If your research specifically concerns DMT vape cartridges, rather than DMT consumption generally, the available statistics are much more limited.
